title: Water system standards: USP, Ph. Eur., ASME BPE | Aquemi
meta: Every standard behind our PW, WFI and pure steam systems: USP <645> 1.3 µS/cm, EN 285, ASME BPE, CSA B51 CRN, and the document that proves each.
eyebrow: COMPLIANCE · USP · PH. EUR. · EU GMP · ASME BPE · CSA B51
headline: Every standard we cite, the number it sets and the document that proves it
lead: Your auditor will ask which standard each design decision answers to, and where the record is. This page lists every standard our system, service and industry pages cite for Purified Water (PW), Water for Injection (WFI) and pure steam: what it governs, the number we design to, the page that shows how, and the document in your turnover package that proves it. Limits are written as the standards state them, from USP <645> conductivity to Canadian registration numbers (CRN) under CSA B51 for pressure equipment. Send your user requirement specification (URS) and we map each requirement to one of these lines.

blocks.h: A standard is a design input, not a certificate
body: USP and Ph. Eur. set limits for water. They do not approve equipment, and no water system is "USP certified". What your inspector accepts is water that meets the monograph at your points of use, measured on qualified instruments, and a record that traces each requirement to a test. We design to the standards below, prove function at the factory acceptance test (FAT), prove performance on your feed water at the site acceptance test (SAT) and operational qualification (OQ), and support your performance qualification (PQ).

The tables are the list we start from. Your URS adds the pharmacopoeias your markets release to, your corporate engineering standard and your province of installation. We write the final list, with editions, into the functional specification so your validation team and ours work from one reference. Where USP and Ph. Eur. differ, we design to the stricter value on each attribute.

blocks.h: Pharmacopoeia and water quality: what each one sets and where the proof sits
cols: The number or requirement we design to
rows: USP <645> Water conductivity
Conductivity of PW and WFI by a three-stage test, and the instrument that measures it

Stage 1: 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C on the non-temperature-compensated reading, with the table limit at the measured temperature rounded down to the 5 °C step. Cell constant known to ± 2 %; instrument accuracy ± 0.1 µS/cm excluding the cell; temperature ± 2 °C
Instrument calibration certificates; executed FAT, SAT and OQ with the raw readings
USP <643> Total organic carbon
TOC of PW and WFI, and the analyzer's system suitability
≤ 0.50 mg/L (500 ppb). System suitability against sucrose and 1,4-benzoquinone standards, acceptance 85–115 % response efficiency
System suitability records; analyzer calibration certificate; OQ report
USP <85> Bacterial endotoxins
The endotoxin test for WFI, and for pure steam condensate used to make parenterals
< 0.25 EU/mL at the point of use
Endotoxin reduction stated in the functional specification; endotoxin results in the PQ sampling plan
USP monographs: Purified Water, Water for Injection, Pure Steam
The grades, their source water and the production route

Made from drinking water. WFI by distillation or by a process equivalent or superior to distillation. Pure steam condensate meets the WFI attributes, with < 0.25 EU/mL endotoxin when the steam is used to make parenterals
Basis of design stating the grade and route for each point of use
USP <1231> Water for pharmaceutical purposes
Informational chapter: system design, sanitization, source water, sampling and microbial control
Microbial action levels of 100 CFU/mL for PW and 10 CFU/100 mL for WFI as generally appropriate maximums. 65–80 °C most commonly used for thermal sanitization
Functional specification; sampling plan; alert and action level rationale
Ph. Eur. 0008 Purified water
The European PW monograph, revised in Ph. Eur. 12.3 (in force 1 July 2026)
≤ 5.1 µS/cm at 25 °C (≤ 4.3 µS/cm at 20 °C); TOC ≤ 0.50 mg/L; nitrates ≤ 0.2 ppm; 100 CFU/mL
Functional specification with the stricter-of basis; nitrates tested at FAT where you release in Europe
Ph. Eur. 0169 Water for injections
The European WFI monograph, including the production route

≤ 1.1 µS/cm at 20 °C (stage 1); < 0.25 IU/mL; 10 CFU/100 mL by membrane filtration of at least 200 mL, R2A agar, 30–35 °C for at least 5 days. Since 1 April 2017, reverse osmosis (RO) coupled with other suitable techniques is accepted, with notice to the GMP supervisory authority before use (EMA/INS/GMP/443117/2017)

The water grade each dosage form, active substance and rinse step needs; in effect since 1 February 2021
WFI for parenterals and biologics; PW as the minimum for most non-sterile dosage forms; final rinse at the grade used for the product

A full year of data; WFI microbial samples of 100 to 300 mL, under 100 mL unacceptable; hot 65–80 °C systems self-sanitizing; double tube sheet to prevent contamination through a leak. Its six-diameter dead leg rule was developed for hot 75–80 °C systems; we design to ASME BPE L/D ≤ 2 instead

blocks.h: Questions validation and quality teams ask

items.a: No water system is. USP and Ph. Eur. set limits for water, not approvals for equipment. Compliance is shown by water at your points of use that meets the monograph, measured on qualified instruments, and by the records behind it. We design to the limits, prove function at FAT and performance on your feed water at SAT and OQ, and hand over the evidence listed on this page.

items.q: Do you design to USP or Ph. Eur.?
items.a: To the stricter value on each attribute when your products ship to both: USP <645> stage 1 for PW conductivity, Ph. Eur. 0008 for nitrates, 0.50 mg/L TOC validated for both. The functional specification names the monographs and editions that apply. The contract manufacturing page sets out each attribute side by side.

items.q: Which edition of each standard do you design to?
items.a: The edition in force when you approve the functional specification, named there. When a text changes during a project, as Ph. Eur. 0008 did in Ph. Eur. 12.3 from 1 July 2026, we assess the change under change control and tell you whether it touches the design, the tests or neither.

items.q: Is your control system 21 CFR Part 11 compliant?
items.a: No system is compliant on its own; your site is, by technical controls in the system plus procedures. We supply the technical controls (audit trail, access control, electronic signatures, record protection and backups) and a written Part 11 and Annex 11 assessment your quality unit can review.

items.q: Who registers our pressure equipment, and when?
items.a: Pressure vessels and fittings installed in Canada need a CRN under CSA B51 from the province of installation. We include registration in the project schedule from the start, because a design built for another market may need changes before it is accepted. [Confirm Aquemi's CRN process and the provinces covered.]

items.q: We have our own corporate engineering standard. Does it replace yours?
items.a: It adds to this list. Send it with the URS: we add it to the standards list in the functional specification and flag any clause that conflicts with a standard here, so your team decides before detailed design, not at IQ.

items.q: Will you complete our supplier questionnaire or quality agreement?
items.a: Send it with the request for proposal. [Confirm Aquemi returns supplier questionnaires and quality agreements with the quote, and the usual turnaround.] The quality management page shows how we control materials, welding, calibration and change.
